close_reason: Done in 48ee0be. Added one paragraph to README §extract_response covering RFC 8620 §3.2 multi-invocation case + error-precedence rule + first-non-error fallback. Refers to function rustdoc for the full contract (JMAP-6r7c.23 method-name caveat included by reference).
description:
extract_response<T>'s function-level rustdoc at client.rs:586-613 explains in detail what happens when multiple invocations share a call_id: 'Errors take precedence. If any invocation matching call_id has method name error, this function returns that error. A success response cannot mask a sibling error response with the same call_id — silently returning the success while the server reported failure would be data loss for the caller.'

This is the semantic that the test suite pins (test_extract_response_error_after_success_takes_precedence at client_tests.rs:958, test_extract_response_first_success_when_no_error at line 999, test_extract_response_error_after_multiple_successes at line 1045).

README.md:308-323 documents extract_response but only says: 'Returns ClientError::MethodError if the server returned a JMAP error response for that call (RFC 8620 §3.6.1).' It does not say what happens when the same call_id has both a success and an error invocation — which is exactly the case for Foo/copy with onSuccessDestroyOriginal:true (RFC 8620 §5.8).

This is a footgun: a downstream consumer wiring extract_response without reading the function-level rustdoc may not realize the error-precedence guarantee. They may write retry logic that assumes success-returned implies no sibling failure occurred.

Fix: one paragraph in the README extract_response section that names the multi-invocation case and the error-precedence rule. Same prose as the function rustdoc is fine.
title: extract_response error-precedence semantic documented on function but not in README API reference
